knowledgePattern: Combine geometric convergence with a trigonometric solution count

hints.title: Sum the geometric series
hints.body: Write down the first term and common ratio of the series. Use the sum-to-infinity formula only where the ratio has size less than 1.
hints.recap: A geometric series has sum <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>/</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>r</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> when <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>r</mi><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mo><</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math>.
hints.pitfall: Also exclude any angle where the tangent on the right is undefined.
hints.pause: Find the sum and write down the excluded angles before rearranging.

recall.reminder: A geometric series has sum <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>/</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>r</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> when <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>r</mi><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mo><</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math>.

hints.title: Write the equation using sine
hints.body: Replace tanx by sinx/cosx and use 1−cos2x=sin2x. Clear denominators only after keeping their excluded values.
hints.recap: The identity <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mi>sin</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>cos</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> lets you use one trigonometric function.
hints.pitfall: A value excluded from the original equation cannot come back after cancellation.
hints.pause: Put <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>u</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>sin</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow></math> and form an equation containing only <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>u</mi></mrow></math>.

recall.reminder: The identity <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mi>sin</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>cos</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> lets you use one trigonometric function.

hints.title: Count without solving the cubic
hints.body: On the same axes, draw y=u3 and y=1−u2 for −1≤u≤1. Check negative and positive u separately.
hints.recap: Intersections of these graphs give the possible sine values.
hints.pitfall: A possible sine value and an angle are different things; count the angles afterwards.
hints.pause: Count the intersections using signs and increasing/decreasing graphs, then count the corresponding angles in the stated interval.

recall.reminder: After finding the possible sine values, count every angle in the specified interval and check excluded values.

solution:
1. The series has first term cosx and ratio cos2x. It converges when cos2x<1. The tangent also requires cosx≠0. Thus exclude x=0,π/2,π,3π/2 in the stated interval.

2. On the remaining domain, the equation is cosx/sin2x=sinx/cosx. Multiplication by the nonzero denominators gives cos2x=sin3x. Put u=sinx to obtain 1−u2=u3.

3. For −1≤u≤0, the two sides have incompatible signs, including the checked endpoints. On [0,1], u3 increases strictly from 0 to 1 while 1−u2 decreases strictly from 1 to 0. They cross exactly once, at an interior level.

4. That sine level lies strictly between 0 and 1 and gives exactly two angles in [0,2π). Both avoid the excluded inputs. Answer C.
